findings.description: Critical: Preflight pruning removes approved/rejected store files and caches, but only a due deferral is specified to bypass the unchanged-fingerprint early exit. A terminal-only prune can therefore re-present the prior digest byte-for-byte even though it still contains the removed terminal candidate, and the freed capacity is not exposed to SENSE.
findings.resolution: Make every lifecycle mutation, including terminal pruning, bypass the unchanged exit and rebuild the digest from surviving caches; add a terminal-only prune scenario proving the stale candidate disappears and newly freed capacity can be used.

findings.description: Critical: The revised plan makes the staleness reference clock host-owned but still never defines the artifact timestamp subtracted from it. candidate-work.schema.json contains no observed/emitted timestamp; filesystem mtime changes across clones and is absent from the cycle fingerprint, so identical trees can receive different staleness penalties.
findings.resolution: Define a reproducible artifact-age source, such as the last Git commit time for a tracked provenance path plus an explicit rule for uncommitted/missing artifacts, or add a canonical source timestamp to the input contract. Test fresh clones, uncommitted evidence, and unchanged fingerprints.

findings.description: Critical: The normative spec still says refiner owns final priority renumbering, while the revised design explicitly says add does not renumber and the consumed _apply_add implementation confirms it. Implementers cannot satisfy both contracts.
findings.resolution: Replace the stale spec clause with the selected explicit-priority behavior and update the --after scenario to assert insertion position and numeric priority independently.

findings.description: Critical: D8 caps the full manifest input at 64 KiB, but the proposal and normative spec cap only evidence; canonical stub title/description/rationale strings have no maximum. The behavior for one schema-valid stub whose payload alone exceeds 64 KiB is undefined, so implementation must either violate the security bound or omit required ranked work.
findings.resolution: Use one term consistently for the complete serialized prompt payload, define byte accounting, and specify fail-closed behavior for an individually oversized stub with a scenario proving it is not dispatched or silently lost.

findings.description: Critical: The plan promises an atomic publish across per-stub caches, digest.json, and supervisor-record.json without defining a transaction, recovery marker, or write order; ordinary atomic file replacement cannot make multiple paths crash-atomic. It also says a failed scoring run retries next cycle without specifying whether cycle-ledger.json advances, which can instead trigger the unchanged early exit and suppress that retry.
findings.resolution: Define an implementable commit protocol, such as staged generation plus one authoritative manifest/pointer and startup recovery, and state that failed scoring does not advance the successful-cycle fingerprint. Add interruption tests at every publish boundary and a next-cycle retry scenario.

findings.description: Critical: Revision 3 selects one bounded batch and a strict all-status dependency index, but implementation instructions still require deterministic chunk/merge behavior and the canonical readiness resolver, and the proposal dependency section still claims ri-16's ready-frontier resolver supplies dependency status. These contradictory instructions can recreate the exact multi-batch and incomplete-readiness defects PLAN_FIX intended to remove.
findings.resolution: Update tasks 1.8 and 2.2, proposal Impact/Dependencies, and all test wording to the single-manifest protocol and name the exact strict loader/archive APIs that build the dependency-status index.

findings.description: Nit: D2 still says ranking constants and buckets are emitted in weights, but digest.schema.json allows only six numeric weight fields and cannot represent the staleness cap, decision/readiness bucket order, risk direction, or stub-key tie-break. A consumer cannot reconstruct the advertised total order from the artifact alone.
findings.resolution: Either extend the schema with explicit ranking-policy fields or narrow the design claim and interpretability requirement to the arithmetic that the artifact actually carries.

findings.description: The revised plan now names a concrete text redactor, rejects unsafe provenance paths, bounds candidate count, and keeps all model dispatch in the host rather than deterministic scripts.
findings.resolution: Retain these boundary checks and negative tests during implementation.

findings.description: The revised work-package scope now includes the new digest, cycle-state, and rubric-prompt runtime mirrors, while preserving an acyclic two-lane dependency graph.
findings.resolution: Retain full-payload mirror verification and DAG checks during implementation.
